notes: Two image modalities of the same blood cells: label-free multi-illumination microscope stacks (LF) and photos of the same cells after Giemsa staining (GS, the clinical standard); 15.7k registered cell pairs on 2 slides. Goal: make LF-trained predictors usable on GS images. a exact-cell retrieval GS -> LF on a held-out slide (rings: slide b1, 5,697 cells / slide b0, 10,015 cells; dashed = chance .00176 (b1); b0 chance .00100), N045 v2 (4,500 steps, seed 0). linear map = ridge regression GS -> LF features fitted on the pairs; SOTAlign = SigLIP pairs + KL-OT on unpaired clinical GS and LF cells. Cross-slide R@10 .01-.04, while the same SigLIP/SOTAlign models reach .40/.38 and .38/.37 within a slide (held-out fields of view; chance .010-.016): the failure is the slide-to-slide shift, not missing shared information. b per-cell signal carried through each complete recipe and compared with its measured value on the same held-out cells (autofluorescence; N045 v5c and N054 truths correlate 1.000): N045 arms = embedding + ridge readout fitted on the source draw; N054 arms (seed 0) = GS students trained to regress the LF model's outputs (output distillation, TT6c) or its latent (LF hub), and a two-space model whose final alignment step is unpaired entropic Gromov-Wasserstein (its GS encoder was trained with pairs); N054 LF training also used unstained cells of the held-out slide. Recipes differ in more than the alignment, so b compares complete pipelines. c learning from set-level supervision with the pairs hidden (N034-B, user idea, one draw, LF features from an encoder that saw the test draw): the LF -> label map is learned only from matched SETS of cells (bag means / 1-D OT); per-cell r on a new blood draw vs set size (mean of 7 targets; 6 at n = 2048, CD19 missing; dashed = fully paired readout .561). Sets of the same cells recover most of the signal at 4-16 cells and decay with set size; sets of different cells carry no per-cell information (r ~ 0).
significance: two-sided; Holm-corrected over all comparisons of a panel (one family per panel); * <0.05 ** <0.01 *** <0.001 **** <0.0001
